chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm from Ibn Bukayr from some of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the grave digger (nabbash): if he is taken the first time, he is flogged (ta'zir); if he returns, he is executed. These final narrations all indicate that the grave digger is only executed if that (repeated digging) is his habit/custom. As for if it is not his habit, he is examined: if he dug and took the shroud, execution is obligatory upon him; and if he did not take it, there is not upon him more than flogging. And upon this we base the narrations that we presented earlier and those that indicate that.

key_terms.الكَفَنَ: The shroud (burial cloth of the deceased)
key_terms.النَّبَّاش: Grave digger (one who digs graves to steal from the dead)
key_terms.عُزِّرَ: He was given ta'zir (discretionary punishment, typically flogging)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment for a grave digger who steals versus one who does not, and when is execution required?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi synthesizes seemingly contradictory reports by distinguishing between habitual grave robbers, who face execution, and first-time offenders, who receive discretionary punishment (ta'zir). He specifically notes that taking the shroud (kafan) mandates execution, while other thefts result in flogging, demonstrating the Shia method of reconciling legal texts through contextual interpretation.
